title: FetchJWTSVID ignores JWTSVIDRequest.spiffe_id and returns a single highest-assurance SVID, contradicting the vendored proto
description:
proto/spiffe/workload/workload.proto:116-123 defines:

  message JWTSVIDRequest {
      repeated string audience = 1;
      // Optional. The requested SPIFFE ID for the JWT-SVID. If unset, all
      // JWT-SVIDs to which the workload is entitled are requested.
      string spiffe_id = 2;
  }

hire-grpc/src/service.rs:224-457 (fetch_jwtsvid) never reads req.spiffe_id. It
proves every candidate from every attestor (:292-322), keeps whichever single
claim has the highest assurance, and returns exactly one SVID (:450-456).

SCOPE NOW: this bead covers the spiffe_id half ONLY. The plural half is decided
and split out -- see persona-jl4j.

(1) spiffe_id set. Trigger: a caller holding several identities asks
specifically for spiffe://ssh.local/key/. It silently receives whichever
identity the daemon ranked highest, with status OK. The caller gets no signal
its selector was discarded.

This is worse to detect than it first looks. The returned spiffe_id is a
PER-CONSUMER PSEUDONYM (service.rs:418-421), not the requested ID, so a caller
comparing the response against what it asked for will not match EITHER WAY. It
cannot tell substitution from normal pseudonymisation by inspection. A caller
that trusts the response and forwards the token authenticates as the wrong
identity to the relying party.

(2) Unspecified tiebreak. The comparison at :317-321 is strictly greater-than
over an unordered iteration of self.attestors, so among equal-assurance claims
the FIRST registered wins. That is not arbitrary today -- it is load-bearing.
Both current provers yield iaa1, and registry.rs appends the unix-account
source last precisely so ssh-agent beats it, which is the behaviour README.md
promises ("added after every probed source, so it wins only when nothing else
proved anything"). Nothing in the type system holds that invariant. Reorder the
registry and every consumer silently gets a different identity.

FIX, per the persona-jl4j decision:
  - Honour req.spiffe_id as a selector; return NOT_FOUND when no proven claim
    matches it. Pre-filtering candidates before prove() is a sound optimisation
    ONLY where it cannot produce a false negative: Candidate::spiffe_id()'s own
    doc comment (claim.rs:92-95) warns that a proven Claim may sit under a
    DIFFERENT trust domain, because a verified token re-anchors it. So
    pre-filter on what cannot move, and make the post-proof match the contract.
  - Specify the tiebreak among equal-assurance claims and test it, so the
    ssh-agent-beats-unix-account behaviour is held by an assertion rather than
    by the order of two push calls in registry.rs.

Returning the LIST rather than one SVID is persona-jl4j.2 and depends on this.
notes: Line numbers refreshed 2026-09-15 against the post-rename tree; the original cited service.rs:99-205 and :120-137, which predate several commits. Scope narrowed to the spiffe_id selector and the tiebreak: the 'return all entitled SVIDs' half is decided under persona-jl4j (return the silently-provable set, sorted, tagged via the proto's own hint field) and tracked as persona-jl4j.2, which depends on this.
